[Nested checked-record Java/Kotlin packages](../evidence/nested-checked-record-jvm-20261016/index.json) establish those positions through generated Java records and Kotlin classes in reproduced, source-free and relocated Maven installations on JDK 22.0.2 and Kotlin 2.2.0. Exact constructor failures preserve caller graphs and later calls recover. Exact constructor failures preserve caller graphs and later calls recover. "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. Generic and recursive records, other indices and dynamic dependent payloads are not covered. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. Generic, recursive and inherited records, other indices and dynamic dependent payloads are not covered. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection."

edits.previous: "note": "Compiled Lean constructs checked inputs through selected safe constructors and projects result payloads. Additional nested C# acceptance: Two independent author builds reproduce the complete NuGet package. Author sources are removed before offline restore; unchanged callers replay after moving the installed tree and execute again after deleting all consumer sources, giving three executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Independent controls reject every missing record and coordinated environment, resource, model, package and execution mutation. Nested checked-record C# acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic, recursive and inherited records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete NuGet packages from two author roots, remove author sources, restore offline, replay after relocation and execute again after deleting all consumer sources. The runs use .NET SDK 8.0.424 and shared framework 8.0.30 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Original packages, receipts, restore inputs, API-probe diagnostics, execution records and selected sources are retained; external toolchain binaries are represented by version, size and digest. Constructor/source entry counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow. Generic and recursive records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as BigInteger values. Holder nests Packet, and ChoicePacket carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Java and Kotlin adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, array, list, option, tuple, result, Holder and Choice input site. edits.previous: "note": "Compiled Lean constructs checked inputs through selected safe constructors and projects result payloads. Additional nested native PHP acceptance: Two independent author builds reproduce the complete Composer ZIP. Author and build roots are removed before offline installation; unchanged weak and strict callers run before and after moving the complete installed tree, giving four executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active ChoicePacket.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Checked-record native PHP acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic, recursive and inherited checked records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete Composer ZIPs from two author roots, remove author and build roots, install offline, and replay unchanged weak and strict callers after relocating each installation. The runs use PHP 8.2.33 and Composer 2.5.5 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor, 64-bit machine words and a recorded 20.0 host-load admission ceiling. The archive retains complete packages, receipts, installed closures, execution records and both producer and verifier source closures. Consumer PHP source remains required at runtime. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the dedicated workflow. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured."

Author and build roots are removed before offline installation; unchanged weak and strict callers run before and after moving the complete installed tree, giving four executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active ChoicePacket.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Checked-record native PHP acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic and recursive checked records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete Composer ZIPs from two author roots, remove author and build roots, install offline, and replay unchanged weak and strict callers after relocating each installation. The runs use PHP 8.2.33 and Composer 2.5.5 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor, 64-bit machine words and a recorded 20.0 host-load admission ceiling. The archive retains complete packages, receipts, installed closures, execution records and both producer and verifier source closures. Consumer PHP source remains required at runtime. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the dedicated workflow. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Additional inherited php acceptance: The php installed lane authenticates the reviewed full inherited checked-record package selection for php-native. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only Composer packages through an independent PHP caller. Complete Composer ZIPs are reproduced, installed offline, executed before and after relocation, and replayed without Lean sources or compilers. Complete package archives, receipts, inventories, probes, execution records, TAP, controls, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. The package floor is glibc 2.38; the archive records and verifies the hosted runner's independently observed glibc and PHP tool identities. Compiler, operating system, PHP interpreter, Composer implementation, native toolchain, and glibc distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed PHP behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. The selected Lean constructor checks or normalizes each input; constructor rejection identifies the parameter and constructor. Calls preserve complete caller inputs, and later valid calls recover. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed Node, page, React and worker checks in all three browser engines. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection."

edits.previous: "note": "Two independent author builds reproduce the complete Maven package. Author sources are removed before offline installation; Java and Kotlin callers replay after moving the installed tree and execute again after deleting all consumer sources, giving six executions per selection. Independent controls reject every missing or changed retained record and coordinated resource, model, package, probe and execution mutations. Checked-record JVM acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic, recursive and inherited records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete Maven packages from two author roots, remove author sources, install offline, replay after relocation and execute again after deleting all consumer sources. The runs use JDK 22.0.2, Kotlin 2.2.0 and Lean 4.32.2 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Original receipts, retained package members, compiler probes, execution records and selected sources are archived; native libraries and the closed JAR retain exact identities without copied bytes. Constructor entry counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow."

The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only CPAN packages through an independent Perl caller. Both prepared archives reproduce from independent author roots, install offline through prebuilt and generated XS modes, execute source-free, relocate, and replay unchanged. Every cell covers threaded and unthreaded Perl 5.36.3 and 5.38.2 interpreters, for sixteen installed executions per selection. Complete CPAN archives, receipts, inventories, execution records, TAP, controls, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. The package floor is glibc 2.38; compiler, operating system, interpreter, native toolchain, and glibc distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed Perl behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed."
